summary: Asked, for the first time, whether mypintusan's offline mode and its cache TTL can actually be observed on a running appliance (tools/fleetbench/bench_pintusan_offline.py, 19 checks over 8 episodes; item 3 of the hardening register for the app that physically opens doors, after Secure Channel and the six alarms). Decide()'s GATE 10 is the app's stated defence against the oldest attack on an access-control system - past the TTL the door denies, and there is deliberately no allow-all option because 'fail open on network loss' is a documented attack (cut the uplink, walk in) - and its unit tests are good, which is exactly the shape that lulls, since the gate can be flawless while nothing on a real controller ever feeds it a number. FOUR DEFECTS, all of the same shape as the six-alarms bench before it: the gate was right and nothing could reach it. (1) THE CACHE COULD NEVER EXPIRE. ControllerConfig.CacheAge was declared and compared against each door's TTL in Decide()'s GATE 10, and nothing assigned it anywhere outside a unit test; in production it was nil, so Snapshot.CacheAge was always zero, so s.CacheAge > ttl was always false, so the reason code offline-cache-expired could not be produced on any install ever. Measured live: a door 20 seconds past a 2-second TTL still granted. Fixed by new apps/mypintusan/services/cache_clock.go (services.CacheClock) - measures the time since anything entitled to change the access rules last reached this controller, persisted in a runtime_setting row (access.lastContact) so a reboot cannot reset staleness to zero, writes throttled to once a minute. Two contact signals reset it: the fleet control channel being live (a new nil-safe SetOnContact hook on domain/shared/fleetnode's control channel, fired on hello and on every parent frame including the keepalive pong), and any accepted administrative change to the access rules on the appliance itself (a new ruleChangeTouch middleware in apps/mypintusan/app/app.go, scoped by path prefix and to 2xx responses only). (2) offlinePolicy: deny AND offlineTtlSeconds WERE UNREACHABLE. createDoorRequest had neither field; the create handler hardcoded OfflinePolicy: entities.OfflineCached and left the TTL at 0 (the class default of 8/24/72 hours). There is no PUT /api/doors, so every door on every install was born cached with a class-default TTL and kept it for good. Both fields are now accepted on create; offlinePolicy is validated to cached|deny and anything else - notably any spelling of allow - is REFUSED with an explicit message rather than silently coerced, because there is no fail-open policy in this product; a negative TTL is refused too. (3) TURNING OFFLINE MODE ON DID NOT REACH THE RUNNING CONTROLLERS. The runtime read Offline once at process start. A PUT /api/settings/access with offline: true persisted, returned 200 and read back true while every door carried on deciding as though online. ControllerConfig.Offline became func() bool (a live question, not a boot-time fact) backed by an atomic on the runtime; IAccessSettingsService gained OnChange, published on Save and Reset; runtime.ApplySettings applies offline live. Only offline applies live - buses, reader keys, timers and the site timezone still need a restart, and the Settings screen's restart note was reworded to name exactly which fields that covers. (4) NOBODY WAS TOLD THE SITE WAS DEGRADED. docs/MYPINTUSAN_DATA_MODEL.md section 2 has said since P1 that a controller serving from cache raises a degraded-mode alert immediately; nothing raised one, and a cached grant is byte-identical to a live one at the door and on every screen. New alarm kind services.AlarmDegraded (degraded), WARNING severity, headline Running from cache - access rules cannot be updated, raised on the transition into offline mode AND at boot for an appliance that starts offline (which never crosses the edge and would otherwise run degraded forever with nobody told). ALSO ADDED: offline mode had no control on the Settings screen at all, so the only way to enable it was editing config.json before first boot; a checkbox was added (settings.offlineHead/offline/offlineHint, translated in en/ms/zh/ar). THE POSITIVE CONTROL IS LOAD-BEARING: episode 3 badges a critical door with a holder not flagged OfflineAllowed and requires the offline-not-allowed denial, which comes from nowhere else in the app - without it, 'the TTL did not deny' and 'the gate never ran at all' would be the same observation. PROVEN GOOD and recorded as such: GATE 10 does run on a live controller; Holder.OfflineAllowed was already reachable via POST /api/holders and works end to end; the access log's offline flag is set correctly; a revoked credential is denied credential-revoked and not masked by a stale cache (reported UNPROVABLE rather than a false pass on a run where the cache never actually expires); and no allow-all offline policy can be created, before or after the fix. TWO THINGS DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT, recorded as open gaps rather than papered over: there is still no PUT /api/doors and no doors-admin screen (doors are only created by the first-run wizard), so the new offline policy fields are reachable through the API only; and there is no replica-refresh mechanism anywhere in the suite - myseliasan pushes no access data down to a node, and no other route does either - so the appliance's own database remains its only authority and offline mode stays an operator-declared deployment mode rather than something the controller detects for itself. docs/MYPINTUSAN_DATA_MODEL.md section 2's old sentence describing the cache as 'a full local replica...refreshed on change' described a topology that never existed and has been corrected to say so. 19/19 checks pass with the fixes; 12/19 against the unfixed app.
compatibility: Backward-compatible; no schema change. Two new fields on POST /api/doors, offlinePolicy and offlineTtlSeconds, both optional - omitting offlinePolicy keeps the existing default (cached) and omitting offlineTtlSeconds keeps the existing class-default TTL (8/24/72 hours for critical/perimeter/interior), so an existing automation or the first-run wizard needs no change. IAccessSettingsService gained an OnChange method; existing callers of the interface are unaffected since it is additive. BEHAVIOURAL CHANGES AN OPERATOR WILL NOTICE, all of them the offline design actually working for the first time: a door's offline cache TTL now genuinely expires and denies with offline-cache-expired once past it, where before it never did; offlinePolicy: deny can now be set and is honoured, where before every door was cached regardless of what was requested; toggling access.offline via Settings now takes effect immediately on every running bus instead of requiring a restart; and enabling offline mode now raises a WARNING-severity access.degraded alert (and one at boot, on an appliance whose config.json already has access.offline: true) where none was ever raised before. A site that has been running with access.offline: true since before this change, or that flips it on for the first time after upgrading, will start seeing this alert - that is the point, and it is the one signal that a controller is running on rules it can no longer be told have changed. NO STOCK INSTALL IS AFFECTED BY ANY OF THAT: the shipped apps/mypintusan/config.json sets access.offline to false, so GATE 10 does not run at all on a default appliance and no door changes behaviour until an operator deliberately turns offline mode on. There is still no PUT /api/doors, so a door's offline policy remains fixed at creation - it is now simply possible to state it there. Scope is `infra` rather than `mypintusan`: mypintusan has no entry in infra/versioning/version.json's apps map yet, and an unknown scope token hard-fails the release run.
